plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Brilliant crimson bracts flare out like stars around tiny yellow-green flower clusters. They light up Mexican hillsides and holiday windowsills alike. The showy 'petals' are actually colored leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (roughly November to February), triggered by the long nights of the short days
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico; also widely grown as a holiday plant around the world
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants. They need long, uninterrupted nights to color up, which is why they peak naturally around Christmas.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree that becomes a canopy of flame-orange and scarlet blossoms. Fern-like leaves sit beneath the flowers, and fallen petals carpet the ground. It is one of the most spectacular of all tropical flowering trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer in the Southern Hemisphere tropics, with main flowering usually beginning in late November or early December
plants.location: Tropical Queensland, Australia (native to Madagascar, widely planted in the tropics)
plants.funFact: In the wild in Madagascar, this tree is endangered, yet it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Rounded globes of trumpet-shaped blue flowers rise on tall, slender stems above strappy, arching leaves. They sway through the midsummer heat along coastal gardens and hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, December to April in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Eastern Cape, South Africa, where it grows wild; widely grown in gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: The name Agapanthus comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'. Despite being called a lily, it belongs to the amaryllis family.
